admission.justification: The strip and the failure-line component together realize the rule. The worker reported the duplicated prose as the cause of the developer's report — the same answer rendered in the strip and in the chat directly below it, with the strip's scroll block taken for a rendering fault — so removing the text removes both the duplication and the false fault.

applicability: The ordinary role launcher bar above the chat in the dashboard's Role chats pane.
conditions: The existing controls remain; configured Step up and receipt-derived model/status badges share their wrapping container.
Result opens its report in the existing reader. A step-up status carries the model and any observed mode from the receipt without exposing reply text or report paths.

Base mode, notes and feature chips are explicitly non-applied previews after step-up. The receipt supplies its model and step-up source. The status shows an observed mode when the receipt supplies one and labels the mode and features unreported when it has no mode observation.

A pending metadata request may show selectable inventory from the matching saved catalogue with remembered scope defaults. An answer for the current generation replaces that inventory when it arrives.
While the displayed model’s options are pending, its selector carries the pending indication and remains selectable.
The catalogue does not add a separate status line to the launcher controls.
exclusions: The chat frame and the messages it shows are outside this obligation.
A host-side rendering fault inside the embedded frame is not text under the launcher's controls.
The removed reply text is not re-offered as a shortened line, a tooltip, an aria-description or a collapsed panel.
statement: The launcher shows its controls, one actionable failure line when needed, and compact receipt-driven step-up identification. The shown model remains selectable while its options are pending. Execution detail, reply text and report paths stay outside the control strip.
